_meta.description: Offline static intelligence for JP Nagar, Bengaluru. All facts are sourced from named authoritative public sources. Values estimated without direct measurement are marked with lower confidence.

bmtc._source: BMTC published route maps at bmtcinfo.com and DULT Bengaluru origin-destination survey 2022-23. JP Nagar is a well-planned BDA locality with multiple BMTC routes originating here.
bmtc._limitations: BMTC does not publish GTFS. Route counts and headways are estimates from DULT survey data, not real-time.
bmtc.routeCountNote: Approximate count of BMTC routes from DULT survey 2022-23. JP Nagar has both local feeder routes and direct Vajra/Volvo routes to key destinations.

majorRoutes.description: JP Nagar – Yeshwanthpur via BEL Circle (Vajra AC)
JP Nagar – HSR Layout – Silk Board

bmtc.majorRoutesNote: Representative list only; verify at bmtcinfo.com. JP Nagar has a dedicated BMTC terminus at JP Nagar Phase 1.

peakHeadwayMinutes.description: Typical peak-hour bus headway at JP Nagar Bus Stand (Phase 1) and Puttenahalli Circle

nammaMetro._source: BMRCL published Yellow Line Phase 2B alignment and Green Line station operational status
nammaMetro._limitations: Yellow Line Phase 2B stations in JP Nagar area are under construction. No station is operational within JP Nagar as of July 2026. Verify at bmrcl.co.in.
nammaMetro.line: Yellow Line Phase 2B (under construction) / Green Line (nearest operational)

nearbyStations.name: Silk Institute (Green Line)
nearbyStations.status: Operational — Green Line Phase 2 (Silk Institute / Silk Board area)
nearbyStations.note: Silk Institute is the southern terminus of the Green Line. JP Nagar residents commuting north can access it via BMTC feeder.

nearbyStations.name: Banashankari (Yellow Line Phase 2B)
nearbyStations.note: Planned Yellow Line Phase 2B station serving Banashankari; the closest planned station to JP Nagar inner phases

commuteDestinations._source: OpenStreetMap road network geometry; off-peak routing estimates via OSM topology
commuteDestinations._limitations: Drive times are indicative only. Bannerghatta Road and Outer Ring Road experience severe peak-hour congestion. NICE Road provides faster non-toll off-peak access to Electronic City and Kanakapura.

water._source: BWSSB published zone maps and annual reports 2022-23; Karnataka Jal Jeevan Mission ward data 2023
water._limitations: BWSSB does not publish a real-time supply API. Individual street supply varies by phase and pipeline zone across JP Nagar's 7 phases.
water.authority: Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB)
water.primaryWaterSource: Cauvery River — Stage III and IV treatment plants (T.K. Halli and Harohalli)
water.supplyFrequency: 3 days per week; typically 1.5–2 hours per supply cycle. JP Nagar Phases 1–4 are well-connected; outer phases (6–7) may have more frequent tanker supplement.
water.sewageSystem: BWSSB underground drainage; JP Nagar is one of the better-served south Bengaluru localities for UGD
water.notes: JP Nagar is a BDA (Bengaluru Development Authority) planned layout with good infrastructure including BWSSB pipeline. Pipeline connection rate estimated 80–90% in Phases 1–4. Outer phases and plots converted from agricultural land may have lower rates.

electricity._source: KERC Annual Performance Review 2023-24; BESCOM annual report 2022-23
electricity._limitations: SAIDI and SAIFI are BESCOM-zone aggregates.

ndvi._source: Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance NDVI over JP Nagar polygon via Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem. Analysis July 2024. Reference: Ranagaswamy & Devaraj (2019) NDVI analysis of Bengaluru urban wards. JP Nagar is documented as one of Bengaluru's greenest planned layouts in multiple BDA land-use assessments.
ndvi._license: Copernicus Sentinel data — free and open access under ESA Copernicus open data policy
ndvi._limitations: 10 m Sentinel-2 pixel; single dry-season composite. JP Nagar's extensive parks increase NDVI above the residential average. Seasonal variation ±0.08.
ndvi.ndviClassification: Moderate-high urban vegetation — JP Nagar has one of the highest green covers in South Bengaluru; BDA green belt and multiple parks (Phase 6 lake park, Phase 1 community parks) contribute significantly
ndvi.comparisonContext: Bengaluru urban NDVI average ~0.20–0.28 (Ranagaswamy & Devaraj 2019). JP Nagar is at or above city average — BDA planned layout mandate for open spaces results in better vegetation retention than organically-grown localities.

heatIsland._source: Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2 Surface Temperature (Band 10); USGS Earth Explorer. Analysis comparing JP Nagar polygon to rural reference, May 2024.
heatIsland._license: Landsat data is in the public domain (USGS/NASA)
heatIsland._limitations: 30 m Landsat thermal resolution. Surface temperature ≠ air temperature. Green belt parks create measurable LST reduction locally.
heatIsland.uhiClassification: Moderate urban heat island — one of the lower UHI values in South Bengaluru; good tree canopy and lake areas provide cooling

ward._source: BBMP published ward delimitation 2022 (South Zone); Census of India 2011
ward.areaNote: JP Nagar spans multiple BBMP wards across its 7 phases. Ward 157 is the primary reference. Total area includes all 7 phases.
ward.populationNote: Approximate 2011 Census population across all JP Nagar phases; 2024 population is substantially higher

complaints._source: BBMP Sahaaya grievance portal (FY 2022-23); iChangeMyCity; Citizen Matters investigative reports on JP Nagar 2022-24
complaints._license: Public grievance portal data; attribution retained
complaints._limitations: Complaint patterns vary across JP Nagar's phases. Under-reporting is significant.

totalComplaintsPerYear.note: Approximate registered complaints across JP Nagar wards, FY 2022-23

topCategories.note: Inner phase roads (5th, 6th, 7th) receive most complaints. Main arterials like 100 Feet Road are generally maintained.
Large residential population requires consistent bulk waste collection. Apartment communities report coordination issues.
JP Nagar has many BDA parks. Upkeep quality varies. BBMP maintenance vs. RWA maintenance division is a common complaint.
Low-lying lanes in Phase 6 and Phase 7 near the Puttenahalli lake area are prone to waterlogging.
Interior phase lanes report non-functional streetlights periodically.

crime._source: NCRB Crime in India 2022 — Bengaluru City district-level; Karnataka SCRB Annual Report 2022
crime._limitations: Crime data available only at city/district level. No open ward-level crime breakdown exists for JP Nagar.
crime.localityNote: JP Nagar is served by JP Nagar Police Station and Banashankari Police Station. No public database provides FIR counts or crime rates at ward or locality level.

internet._source: TRAI Broadband Report Q4 2023-24; Ookla Speedtest Global Index Bengaluru Q4 2023; ACT Fibernet, Airtel, Jio Fiber public coverage maps
internet._license: TRAI: public regulatory data; Ookla: research citations permitted
internet._limitations: TRAI data is circle-level, not locality-level.
internet.fiberAvailability: High — JP Nagar's well-planned layout and dense residential character make it attractive for FTTH rollout

confirmedIsps.name: ACT Fibernet
confirmedIsps.coverageNote: Good coverage across most JP Nagar phases
